name: Afghanistan
dtm_stage: Stage 2 · Death rate falling, birth rate high
terrain: mostly rugged mountains; plains in north and southwest
climate_text: arid to semiarid; cold winters and hot summers
hazards_text: damaging earthquakes occur in Hindu Kush mountains; flooding; droughts

name: Albania
dtm_stage: Stage 4 · Low birth and death rates
terrain: mostly mountains and hills; small plains along coast
climate_text: mild temperate; cool, cloudy, wet winters; hot, clear, dry summers; interior is cooler and wetter
hazards_text: destructive earthquakes; tsunamis occur along southwestern coast; floods; drought

name: Algeria
terrain: mostly high plateau and desert; Atlas Mountains in the far north and Hoggar Mountains in the south; narrow, discontinuous coastal plain
climate_text: arid to semiarid; mild, wet winters with hot, dry summers along coast; drier with cold winters and hot summers on high plateau; sirocco is a hot, dust/sand-laden wind especially common in summer
hazards_text: mountainous areas subject to severe earthquakes; mudslides and floods in rainy season; droughts

name: American Samoa
terrain: five volcanic islands with rugged peaks and limited coastal plains, two coral atolls (Rose Atoll, Swains Island)
climate_text: tropical marine, moderated by southeast trade winds; annual rainfall averages about 3 m; rainy season (November to April), dry season (May to October); little seasonal temperature variation
hazards_text: cyclones common from December to March. Volcanoes: limited volcanic activity on the Ofu and Olosega Islands; neither has erupted since the 19th century

name: Andorra
dtm_stage: Stage 4 · Low birth and death rates
terrain: rugged mountains dissected by narrow valleys
climate_text: temperate; snowy, cold winters and warm, dry summers
hazards_text: avalanches

name: Angola
dtm_stage: Stage 2 · Death rate falling, birth rate high
terrain: narrow coastal plain rises abruptly to vast interior plateau
climate_text: semiarid in south and along coast to Luanda; north has cool, dry season (May to October) and hot, rainy season (November to April)
hazards_text: locally heavy rainfall causes periodic flooding on the plateau

name: Anguilla
terrain: flat and low-lying island of coral and limestone
climate_text: tropical; moderated by northeast trade winds
hazards_text: frequent hurricanes and other tropical storms (July to October)

name: Antarctica
terrain: about 99% thick continental ice sheet and 1% barren rock, with average elevations between 2,000 and 4,000 m; mountain ranges up to nearly 5,000 m; ice-free coastal areas include parts of southern Victoria Land, Wilkes Land, the Antarctic Peninsula area, and parts of Ross Island on McMurdo Sound; glaciers form ice shelves along about half of the coastline, and floating ice shelves constitute 11% of the area of the continent
climate_text: the coldest, windiest, and driest continent on Earth; severe low temperatures vary with latitude, elevation, and distance from the ocean; East Antarctica is colder than West Antarctica because of its higher elevation; Antarctic Peninsula has the most moderate climate; higher temperatures occur in January along the coast and average slightly below freezing; summers characterized by continuous daylight, while winters bring continuous darkness; persistent high pressure over the interior brings dry, subsiding air that results in very little cloud cover
hazards_text: katabatic (gravity-driven) winds blow coastward from the high interior; frequent blizzards form near the foot of the plateau; cyclonic storms form over the ocean and move clockwise along the coast; large icebergs may calve from ice shelf. Volcanoes: volcanic activity on Deception Island and isolated areas of West Antarctica; other seismic activity rare and weak

name: Antigua and Barbuda
dtm_stage: Stage 4 · Low birth and death rates
quake_max_place: near Saint John’s, Antigua and Barbuda
terrain: mostly low-lying limestone and coral islands, with some higher volcanic areas
climate_text: tropical maritime; little seasonal temperature variation
hazards_text: hurricanes and tropical storms (July to October); periodic droughts

name: Argentina
dtm_stage: Stage 4 · Low birth and death rates
terrain: rich plains of the Pampas in northern half, flat to rolling plateau of Patagonia in south, rugged Andes along western border
climate_text: mostly temperate; arid in southeast; subantarctic in southwest
hazards_text: San Miguel de Tucumán and Mendoza areas in the Andes subject to earthquakes; pamperos are violent windstorms that can strike the pampas and northeast; heavy flooding in some areas. Volcanoes: volcanic activity in the Andes Mountains along the Chilean border; Copahue (2,997 m) last erupted in 2000; other historically active volcanoes include Llullaillaco, Maipo, Planchón-Peteroa, San José, Tromen, Tupungatito, and Viedma

name: Armenia
dtm_stage: Stage 4 · Low birth and death rates
terrain: Armenian Highland with mountains; little forest land; fast flowing rivers; good soil in Aras River valley
climate_text: highland continental, hot summers, cold winters
hazards_text: occasionally severe earthquakes; droughts

name: Aruba
terrain: flat with a few hills; scant vegetation
climate_text: tropical marine; little seasonal temperature variation
hazards_text: hurricanes; lies outside the Caribbean hurricane belt and is rarely threatened

name: Australia
dtm_stage: Stage 4 · Low birth and death rates
terrain: mostly low plateau with deserts; fertile plain in southeast
climate_text: generally arid to semiarid; temperate in south and east; tropical in north
hazards_text: cyclones along the coast; severe droughts; forest fires. Volcanoes: volcanic activity on Heard and McDonald Islands

name: Austria
terrain: low with sand and coral
climate_text: tropical
hazards_text: surrounded by shoals and reefs that can pose maritime hazards

name: Azerbaijan
dtm_stage: Stage 4 · Low birth and death rates
terrain: large, flat Kur-Araz Ovaligi (Kura-Araks Lowland, much of it below sea level) with Great Caucasus Mountains to the north, Qarabag Yaylasi (Karabakh Upland) to the west; Baku lies on Abseron Yasaqligi (Apsheron Peninsula) that juts into Caspian Sea
climate_text: dry, semiarid steppe
hazards_text: droughts

name: Bahamas
dtm_stage: Stage 4 · Low birth and death rates

name: Bahrain
dtm_stage: Stage 4 · Low birth and death rates
terrain: mostly low desert plain rising gently to low central escarpment
climate_text: arid; mild, pleasant winters; very hot, humid summers
hazards_text: periodic droughts; dust storms

name: Bangladesh
terrain: mostly flat alluvial plain; hilly in southeast
climate_text: tropical; mild winter (October to March); hot, humid summer (March to June); humid, warm rainy monsoon (June to October)
hazards_text: droughts; cyclones; much of the country routinely inundated during the summer monsoon season

name: Barbados
dtm_stage: Stage 4 · Low birth and death rates
terrain: relatively flat; rises gently to central highland region
climate_text: tropical; rainy season (June to October)
hazards_text: infrequent hurricanes; periodic landslides

name: Belarus
terrain: generally flat with much marshland
climate_text: cold winters, cool and moist summers; transitional between continental and maritime
hazards_text: large tracts of marshy land

name: Belgium
terrain: flat coastal plains in northwest, central rolling hills, rugged mountains of Ardennes Forest in southeast
climate_text: temperate; mild winters, cool summers; rainy, humid, cloudy
hazards_text: flooding is a threat along rivers and in areas of reclaimed coastal land, protected from the sea by concrete dikes

name: Belize
terrain: flat, swampy coastal plain; low mountains in south
climate_text: tropical; very hot and humid; rainy season (May to November); dry season (February to May)
hazards_text: frequent, devastating hurricanes (June to November) and coastal flooding (especially in south)

name: Benin
dtm_stage: Stage 2 · Death rate falling, birth rate high
terrain: mostly flat to undulating plain; some hills and low mountains
climate_text: tropical; hot, humid in south; semiarid in north
hazards_text: hot, dry, dusty harmattan wind may affect north from December to March

name: Bermuda
terrain: low hills separated by fertile depressions
climate_text: subtropical; mild, humid; gales, strong winds common in winter
hazards_text: hurricanes (June to November)

name: Bhutan
dtm_stage: Stage 4 · Low birth and death rates
terrain: mostly mountainous with some fertile valleys and savanna
climate_text: varies; tropical in southern plains; cool winters and hot summers in central valleys; severe winters and cool summers in Himalayas
hazards_text: violent storms from the Himalayas are the source of the country's Bhutanese name, which translates as Land of the Thunder Dragon; frequent landslides during the rainy season

name: Bolivia
terrain: rugged Andes Mountains with a highland plateau (Altiplano), hills, lowland plains of the Amazon Basin
climate_text: varies with altitude; humid and tropical to cold and semiarid
hazards_text: flooding in the northeast (March to April). Volcanoes: volcanic activity in Andes Mountains on the border with Chile; historically active volcanoes in this region are Irruputuncu (5,163 m), which last erupted in 1995, and the Olca-Paruma volcanic complex (5,762 m to 5,167 m)

name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
terrain: mountains and valleys
climate_text: hot summers and cold winters; areas of high elevation have short, cool summers and long, severe winters; mild, rainy winters along coast
hazards_text: destructive earthquakes

name: Botswana
lowest_point: junction of the Limpopo and Shashe Rivers
terrain: predominantly flat to gently rolling tableland; Kalahari Desert in southwest
climate_text: semiarid; warm winters and hot summers
hazards_text: periodic droughts; seasonal August winds blow from the west, carrying sand and dust across the country, which can obscure visibility

name: Bouvet Island
terrain: volcanic; coast is mostly inaccessible
climate_text: antarctic
hazards_text: occasional volcanism, rock slides; harsh climate, surrounded by pack ice in winter

name: Brazil
dtm_stage: Stage 4 · Low birth and death rates
terrain: mostly flat to rolling lowlands in north; some plains, hills, mountains, and narrow coastal belt
climate_text: mostly tropical, but temperate in south
hazards_text: recurring droughts in northeast; floods and occasional frost in south

name: British Indian Ocean Territory
terrain: flat and low coral atolls (most areas do not exceed 2 m, or 6.6 ft, in elevation); sits atop the submarine volcanic Chagos-Laccadive Ridge
climate_text: tropical marine; hot, humid, moderated by trade winds
hazards_text: none; located outside routes of Indian Ocean cyclones

name: British Virgin Islands
dtm_stage: Stage 4 · Low birth and death rates
terrain: coral islands relatively flat; volcanic islands steep, hilly
climate_text: subtropical; humid; temperatures moderated by trade winds
hazards_text: hurricanes and tropical storms (July to October)

name: Brunei
aliases: Nation of Brunei, Abode of Peace
dtm_stage: Stage 4 · Low birth and death rates
terrain: flat coastal plain rises to mountains in east; hilly lowland in west
climate_text: tropical; hot, humid, rainy
hazards_text: typhoons, earthquakes, and severe flooding are rare

name: Bulgaria
terrain: mostly mountains with lowlands in north and southeast
climate_text: temperate; cold, damp winters; hot, dry summers
hazards_text: earthquakes; landslides

name: Burkina Faso
dtm_stage: Stage 2 · Death rate falling, birth rate high
terrain: mostly flat to dissected, undulating plains; hills in the west and southeast; occupies an extensive plateau with savanna that is grassy in the north and gradually gives way to sparse forests in the south
climate_text: three climate zones including a hot tropical savanna with a short rainy season in the southern half, a tropical hot semi-arid steppe climate typical of the Sahel region in the northern half, and small area of hot desert in the very north of the country bordering the Sahara Desert
hazards_text: recurring droughts

name: Burundi
dtm_stage: Stage 2 · Death rate falling, birth rate high
terrain: hilly and mountainous, dropping to a plateau in east, some plains
climate_text: equatorial; high plateau with considerable altitude variation (772 m to 2,670 m above sea level); average annual temperature varies with altitude from 23 to 17 degrees Celsius but is generally moderate; average annual rainfall is about 150 cm with two wet seasons (February to May and September to November) and two dry seasons (June to August and December to January)
hazards_text: flooding; landslides; drought

name: Cambodia
terrain: mostly low, flat plains; mountains in southwest and north
climate_text: tropical; rainy, monsoon season (May to November); dry season (December to April); little seasonal temperature variation
hazards_text: monsoonal rains (June to November); flooding; occasional droughts

name: Cameroon
dtm_stage: Stage 2 · Death rate falling, birth rate high
terrain: diverse, with coastal plain in southwest, dissected plateau in center, mountains in west, plains in north
climate_text: varies with terrain, from tropical along coast to semiarid and hot in north
hazards_text: volcanic activity with periodic releases of poisonous gases from Lake Nyos and Lake Monoun volcanoes. Volcanoes: Mt. Cameroon (4,095 m), which last erupted in 2000, is the most frequently active volcano in West Africa; lakes in the Oku volcanic field sometimes release fatal levels of gas, which killed about 1,700 people in 1986

name: Canada
dtm_stage: Stage 4 · Low birth and death rates
terrain: mostly plains with mountains in west, lowlands in southeast
climate_text: varies from temperate in south to subarctic and arctic in north
hazards_text: continuous permafrost in north is a serious obstacle to development; cyclonic storms form east of the Rocky Mountains, a result of the mixing of air masses from the Arctic, Pacific, and North American interior, and produce most of the country's rain and snow east of the mountains. Volcanoes: the vast majority of volcanoes in Western Canada's Coast Mountains remain dormant

name: Cape Verde
dtm_stage: Stage 4 · Low birth and death rates
terrain: steep, rugged, rocky, volcanic
climate_text: temperate; warm, dry summer; precipitation meager and erratic
hazards_text: prolonged droughts; seasonal harmattan wind produces obscuring dust; volcanically and seismically active. Volcanoes: Fogo (2,829 m), which last erupted in 1995, is Cabo Verde's only active volcano

name: Cayman Islands
dtm_stage: Stage 4 · Low birth and death rates
highest_point: 1 km SW of The Bluff on Cayman Brac
terrain: low-lying limestone base surrounded by coral reefs
climate_text: tropical marine; warm, rainy summers (May to October) and cool, relatively dry winters (November to April)
hazards_text: hurricanes (July to November)

name: Central African Republic
dtm_stage: Stage 2 · Death rate falling, birth rate high
terrain: vast, flat to rolling plateau; scattered hills in northeast and southwest
climate_text: tropical; hot, dry winters; mild to hot, wet summers
hazards_text: hot, dry, dusty harmattan winds affect northern areas; floods are common

name: Chad
dtm_stage: Stage 2 · Death rate falling, birth rate high
terrain: broad, arid plains in center, desert in north, mountains in northwest, lowlands in south
climate_text: tropical in south, desert in north
hazards_text: hot, dry, dusty harmattan winds occur in north; periodic droughts; locust plagues

name: Chile
dtm_stage: Stage 4 · Low birth and death rates
terrain: low coastal mountains, fertile central valley, rugged Andes in east
climate_text: temperate; desert in north; Mediterranean in central region; cool and damp in south
hazards_text: severe earthquakes; active volcanism; tsunamis. Volcanoes: significant volcanic activity due to more than three-dozen active volcanoes along the Andes Mountains; Lascar (5,592 m), which last erupted in 2007, is the most active volcano in the northern Chilean Andes; Llaima (3,125 m) in central Chile, which last erupted in 2009, is another of the country's most active; Chaiten's 2008 eruption forced major evacuations; other notable historically active volcanoes include Cerro Hudson, Calbuco, Copahue, Guallatiri, Llullaillaco, Nevados de Chillan, Puyehue, San Pedro, and Villarrica; see note 2 under "Geography - note"

name: China
terrain: mostly mountains, high plateaus, deserts in west; plains, deltas, and hills in east
climate_text: extremely diverse; tropical in south to subarctic in north
hazards_text: frequent typhoons (about five per year along southern and eastern coasts); damaging floods; tsunamis; earthquakes; droughts; land subsidence. Volcanoes: China contains some historically active volcanoes including Changbaishan (also known as Baitoushan, Baegdu, or P'aektu-san), Hainan Dao, and Kunlun although most have been relatively inactive in recent centuries

name: Christmas Island
terrain: steep cliffs along coast rise abruptly to central plateau
climate_text: tropical with a wet season (December to April) and dry season; heat and humidity moderated by trade winds
hazards_text: the narrow fringing reef surrounding the island can be a maritime hazard

name: Cocos (Keeling) Islands
terrain: flat, low-lying coral atolls
climate_text: tropical with high humidity, moderated by the southeast trade winds for about nine months of the year
hazards_text: cyclone season is October to April

name: Colombia
dtm_stage: Stage 4 · Low birth and death rates
quake_max_place: near San Antonio del Estrecho, Peru
terrain: flat coastal lowlands, central highlands, high Andes Mountains, eastern lowland plains (Llanos)
climate_text: tropical along coast and eastern plains; cooler in highlands
hazards_text: highlands subject to volcanic eruptions; occasional earthquakes; periodic droughts. Volcanoes: Galeras (4,276 m) is one of Colombia's most active volcanoes; it has been deemed a Decade Volcano by the International Association of Volcanology and Chemistry of the Earth's Interior, worthy of study due to its explosive history and close proximity to human populations; Nevado del Ruiz (5,321 m), 129 km (80 mi) west of Bogota, erupted in 1985, producing lahars (mudflows) that killed 23,000 people; the volcano last erupted in 1991; after 500 years of dormancy, Nevado del Huila reawakened in 2007 and has experienced frequent eruptions since then; other historically active volcanoes include Cumbal, Dona Juana, Nevado del Tolima, and Purace

name: Comoros
dtm_stage: Stage 2 · Death rate falling, birth rate high
terrain: volcanic islands, interiors vary from steep mountains to low hills
climate_text: tropical marine; rainy season (November to May)
hazards_text: cyclones possible during rainy season (December to April); volcanic activity on Grand Comore. Volcanoes: Karthala (2,361 m) on Grand Comore Island last erupted in 2007; a 2005 eruption forced thousands of people to be evacuated and produced a large ash cloud

name: Cook Islands
terrain: low coral atolls in north; volcanic, hilly islands in south
climate_text: tropical oceanic; moderated by trade winds; a dry season from April to November and a more humid season from December to March
hazards_text: tropical cyclones (November to March)

name: Costa Rica
dtm_stage: Stage 4 · Low birth and death rates
terrain: sand and coral reefs and islands (cays)
climate_text: tropical
hazards_text: occasional tropical cyclones

name: Croatia
terrain: geographically diverse; flat plains along Hungarian border, low mountains and highlands near Adriatic coastline and islands
climate_text: Mediterranean and continental; continental climate predominant with hot summers and cold winters; mild winters, dry summers along coast
hazards_text: destructive earthquakes

name: Cuba
terrain: mostly flat to rolling plains, with rugged hills and mountains in the southeast
climate_text: tropical; moderated by trade winds; dry season (November to April); rainy season (May to October)
hazards_text: the east coast is subject to hurricanes from August to November (in general, the country averages about one hurricane every other year); droughts are common

name: Curaçao
terrain: generally low, hilly terrain
climate_text: tropical marine climate, ameliorated by northeast trade winds, results in mild temperatures; semiarid with average rainfall of 60 cm/year
hazards_text: Curacao is south of the Caribbean hurricane belt and is rarely threatened

name: Cyprus
dtm_stage: Stage 4 · Low birth and death rates
terrain: central plain with mountains to north and south; scattered but significant plains along southern coast
climate_text: temperate; Mediterranean with hot, dry summers and cool winters
hazards_text: moderate earthquake activity; droughts

name: Czechia
terrain: Bohemia in the west consists of rolling plains, hills, and plateaus surrounded by low mountains; Moravia in the east consists of very hilly country
climate_text: temperate; cool summers; cold, cloudy, humid winters
hazards_text: flooding

name: DR Congo
aliases: Congo, the Democratic Republic of the
dtm_stage: Stage 2 · Death rate falling, birth rate high
terrain: vast central basin is a low-lying plateau; mountains in east
climate_text: tropical; hot and humid in equatorial river basin; cooler and drier in southern highlands; cooler and wetter in eastern highlands; north of Equator - wet season (April to October), dry season (December to February); south of Equator - wet season (November to March), dry season (April to October)
hazards_text: periodic droughts in south; Congo River floods (seasonal); active volcanoes in the east along the Great Rift Valley. Volcanoes: the active volcano Nyiragongo (3,470 m) poses a major threat to the city of Goma, home to a quarter of a million people; it produces unusually fast-moving lava, known to travel up to 100 km/hr; Nyiragongo has been deemed a Decade Volcano by the International Association of Volcanology and Chemistry of the Earth's Interior, worthy of study due to its explosive history and close proximity to human populations; its neighbor Nyamuragira is Africa's most active volcano; Visoke is the only other historically active volcano

name: Denmark
terrain: low and flat to gently rolling plains
climate_text: temperate; humid and overcast; mild, windy winters and cool summers
hazards_text: flooding is a threat in some areas of the country (e.g., parts of Jutland, along the southern coast of the island of Lolland) that are protected from the sea by a system of dikes

name: Djibouti
terrain: coastal plain and plateau separated by central mountains
climate_text: desert; torrid, dry
hazards_text: earthquakes; droughts; occasional cyclonic disturbances from the Indian Ocean bring heavy rains and flash floods. Volcanoes: experiences limited volcanic activity; Ardoukoba (298 m) last erupted in 1978; Manda-Inakir, located along the Ethiopian border, is also historically active

name: Dominica
terrain: rugged mountains of volcanic origin
climate_text: tropical; moderated by northeast trade winds; heavy rainfall
hazards_text: flash floods are a constant threat; destructive hurricanes can be expected during the late summer months. Volcanoes: Dominica lies in the middle of the volcanic-island arc of the Lesser Antilles that extends from the island of Saba in the north to Grenada in the south; of the 16 volcanoes that make up this arc, five are located on Dominica, more than any other island in the Caribbean: Morne aux Diables (861 m), Morne Diablotins (1,430 m), Morne Trois Pitons (1,387 m), Watt Mountain (1,224 m), which last erupted in 1997, and Morne Plat Pays (940 m); the two best-known volcanic features on Dominica, the Valley of Desolation and the Boiling Lake thermal areas, lie on the flanks of Watt Mountain, and both are popular tourist destinations

name: Ecuador
dtm_stage: Stage 4 · Low birth and death rates
terrain: coastal plain (costa), inter-Andean central highlands (sierra), and flat to rolling eastern jungle (oriente)
climate_text: tropical along coast, becoming cooler inland at higher elevations; tropical in Amazonian jungle lowlands
hazards_text: frequent earthquakes; landslides; volcanic activity; floods; periodic droughts. Volcanoes: volcanic activity concentrated along the Andes Mountains; Sangay (5,230 m) is mainland Ecuador's most active volcano; other historically active volcanoes in the Andes include Antisana, Cayambe, Chacana, Cotopaxi, Guagua Pichincha, Reventador, Sumaco, and Tungurahua; Fernandina (1,476 m), a shield volcano, is the most active of the many Galapagos volcanoes; other historically active Galapagos volcanoes include Wolf, Sierra Negra, Cerro Azul, Pinta, Marchena, and Santiago

name: Egypt
terrain: vast desert plateau interrupted by Nile valley and delta
climate_text: desert; hot, dry summers with moderate winters
hazards_text: periodic droughts; frequent earthquakes; flash floods; landslides; hot, driving windstorms called khamsin occur in spring; dust storms; sandstorms

name: El Salvador
terrain: mostly mountains with narrow coastal belt and central plateau
climate_text: tropical; rainy season (May to October); dry season (November to April); tropical on coast; temperate in uplands
hazards_text: known as the Land of Volcanoes; frequent and sometimes destructive earthquakes and volcanic activity; extremely susceptible to hurricanes. Volcanoes: significant volcanic activity; San Salvador (1,893 m), which last erupted in 1917, has the potential to cause major harm to the country's capital, which lies just below the volcano's slopes; San Miguel (2,130 m) is one of the most active volcanoes in the country; other historically active volcanoes include Conchaguita, Ilopango, Izalco, and Santa Ana

name: Equatorial Guinea
dtm_stage: Stage 2 · Death rate falling, birth rate high
terrain: coastal plains rise to interior hills; islands are volcanic
climate_text: tropical; always hot, humid
hazards_text: violent windstorms; flash floods. Volcanoes: Santa Isabel (3,007 m), which last erupted in 1923, is the country's only historically active volcano; Santa Isabel and two dormant volcanoes form Bioko Island in the Gulf of Guinea

name: Eritrea
dtm_stage: Stage 2 · Death rate falling, birth rate high
lowest_point: near Kulul within the Danakil Depression
terrain: dominated by extension of Ethiopian north-south trending highlands, descending on the east to a coastal desert plain, on the northwest to hilly terrain and on the southwest to flat-to-rolling plains
climate_text: hot, dry desert strip along Red Sea coast; cooler and wetter in the central highlands (up to 61 cm of rainfall annually, heaviest June to September); semiarid in western hills and lowlands
hazards_text: frequent droughts, rare earthquakes and volcanoes; locust swarms. Volcanoes: Dubbi (1,625 m), which last erupted in 1861, was the country's only historically active volcano until Nabro (2,218 m) came to life in 2011

name: Estonia
terrain: marshy, lowlands; flat in the north, hilly in the south
climate_text: maritime; wet, moderate winters, cool summers
hazards_text: sometimes flooding occurs in the spring

name: Eswatini
terrain: mostly mountains and hills; some moderately sloping plains
climate_text: varies from tropical to near temperate
hazards_text: drought

name: Ethiopia
dtm_stage: Stage 2 · Death rate falling, birth rate high
terrain: high plateau with central mountain range divided by Great Rift Valley
climate_text: tropical monsoon with wide topographic-induced variation
hazards_text: geologically active Great Rift Valley susceptible to earthquakes, volcanic eruptions; frequent droughts. Volcanoes: volcanic activity in the Great Rift Valley; Erta Ale (613 m) is the country's most active volcano; Dabbahu became active in 2005, forcing evacuations; other historically active volcanoes include Alayta, Dalaffilla, Dallol, Dama Ali, Fentale, Kone, Manda Hararo, and Manda-Inakir

name: Falkland Islands
terrain: rocky, hilly, mountainous with some boggy, undulating plains
climate_text: cold marine; strong westerly winds, cloudy, humid; rain occurs on more than half of days in year; average annual rainfall is 60 cm in Stanley; occasional snow all year, except in January and February, but typically does not accumulate
hazards_text: strong winds persist throughout the year

name: Faroe Islands
dtm_stage: Stage 4 · Low birth and death rates
terrain: rugged, rocky, some low peaks; cliffs along most of coast
climate_text: mild winters, cool summers; usually overcast; foggy, windy
hazards_text: strong winds and heavy rains can occur throughout the year

name: Fiji
terrain: mostly mountains of volcanic origin
climate_text: tropical marine; only slight seasonal temperature variation
hazards_text: cyclonic storms can occur from November to January

name: Finland
terrain: mostly low, flat to rolling plains interspersed with lakes and low hills
climate_text: cold temperate; potentially subarctic but comparatively mild because of moderating influence of the North Atlantic Current, Baltic Sea, and more than 60,000 lakes
hazards_text: severe winters in the north

name: France
dtm_stage: Stage 4 · Low birth and death rates
terrain: metropolitan France: mostly flat plains or gently rolling hills in north and west; remainder is mountainous, especially Pyrenees in south, Alps in east French Guiana: low-lying coastal plains rising to hills and small mountains Guadeloupe: Basse-Terre is volcanic in origin with interior mountains; Grande-Terre is low limestone formation; most of the seven other islands are volcanic in origin Martinique: mountainous with indented coastline; dormant volcano Mayotte: generally undulating, with deep ravines and ancient volcanic peaks Reunion: mostly rugged and mountainous; fertile lowlands along coast
climate_text: metropolitan France: generally cool winters and mild summers, but mild winters and hot summers along the Mediterranean; occasional strong, cold, dry, north-to-northwesterly wind known as the mistral
hazards_text: metropolitan France: flooding; avalanches; midwinter windstorms; drought; forest fires in south overseas departments: hurricanes (cyclones); flooding. Volcanoes: Montagne Pelée (1,394 m) on the island of Martinique in the Caribbean is the most active volcano of the Lesser Antilles arc, although it last erupted in 1932; a catastrophic eruption in 1902 destroyed the city of St. Pierre, killing an estimated 30,000 people; La Soufrière (1,467 m) on the island of Guadeloupe has also had explosive eruptions in recent years

name: French Polynesia
dtm_stage: Stage 4 · Low birth and death rates
terrain: mixture of rugged high islands and low islands with reefs
climate_text: tropical, but moderate
hazards_text: occasional cyclonic storms in January

name: French Southern and Antarctic Lands
